I ran a zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE) on a line of 6 spins. All 6 spins started pointing up. I evolved them under H = (sum of Z Z on neighbors) + (sum of X) to time 1. The evolution used 4 Trotter steps of 0.25 each, which comes to 40 two-qubit CZ gates after compiling to Garnet. I built 3 versions of the circuit. The first is the plain circuit U. The second is U, then U undone (U-dagger), then U again. The third repeats the undo-and-redo pair twice. On a perfect machine all 3 give the same answer. On a real machine the longer ones pick up 3 times and 5 times as much gate noise. They have 40, 120, and 200 CZ gates.

I sent all 3 circuits as one job (ID 01a16042-6f5c-7148-a123-37852856a876, 1000 shots each) to garnet:mock. The job finished with status DONE, so IQM's server accepted the circuits. It cost 0 credits. The mock device returns placeholder counts that do not depend on the circuit, so I did not use them for physics. I then ran the same 3 circuits through IQMFakeGarnet, which is IQM's noisy simulator of Garnet. I used 20,000 shots each.

Magnetization is the average spin direction. It is +1 if every spin points up. The noisy values were 0.1545 at 1x noise, 0.1187 at 3x, and 0.0906 at 5x. More noise pulls the value toward 0. I fit a quadratic curve through the 3 points and read it at zero noise (Richardson extrapolation). The zero-noise estimate is 0.1753. The ideal value for this circuit is 0.1869, from an exact noiseless calculation. The raw 1x result was off by 0.032. The extrapolated result is off by 0.012, which cuts the error by about 63 percent. A straight-line fit gives 0.169 and an exponential fit gives 0.177. These agree with the quadratic fit to within about 0.01.

The principle is that you cannot remove noise from the machine, but you can turn it up on purpose. You measure how the answer changes as the noise grows, then work backward to what a noise-free machine would give. IBM's 2023 utility experiment used this idea. One more note: the exact continuous-time answer is 0.2044. The gap between 0.1869 and 0.2044 comes from splitting the evolution into 4 steps. It is not hardware noise, so ZNE does not correct it.
